public_rationale: The money part cannot be checked. Google did not publish per-prompt cost or revenue for its generative AI products. Pichai said per-query costs fell sharply but gave no margin figure. On interest, a court exhibit showed Gemini at about 90 million monthly and 9 million daily users in October 2024. That is far behind ChatGPT's 400 million weekly users and Meta AI's near 500 million monthly, which fits the speaker's point that uptake was weak for Google's size. But 90 million is not 'nobody', and the speaker himself softened this to 'not that many'. The interest part is partly supported under the relative reading he intended. The per-prompt loss claim, the firmer half, has no public evidence either way. So the claim as a whole stays unresolved.
limitations: User counts come from a news report of a court slide, not the exhibit itself.
Methods for counting users differ across companies.
No per-prompt financial data exist publicly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google loses money on every generative AI prompt, and few people care about Gemini.

statement.excerpt: But Google, like every single other generative AI player, is losing money on every single generative AI prompt, and based on these monthly active user numbers, nobody really cares about Gemini.

from_speaker: Google, like every single other generative AI player
is losing money on every single generative AI prompt
based on these monthly active user numbers
judged against Google's scale and search dominance (context)
next paragraph walks back: 'Some people care about Gemini — not that many, but some!'
our_interpretation: Two parts. Part 1 (money): at the time of the post, the cost of serving a typical Google generative AI prompt was higher than the revenue that prompt brought in, across Google's generative AI products.
Part 2 (interest): Gemini uptake was small relative to Google's reach. The speaker's own next paragraph narrows 'nobody' to 'not that many', so the fair reading is relative, not literal zero.

The claim describes a present state with no period named. Target period: October 2024 to February 2025. That is Google's latest reported quarter (Q4 2024) plus the months up to the post, which his Similarweb and Sensor Tower figures also cover.
criteria.support_condition: Part 1: a credible disclosure or estimate showing Google's per-prompt serving cost was above per-prompt revenue across its generative AI products in the period. Part 2: Gemini usage that was clearly small next to Google's reach and next to rival chatbots in the period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Part 1: credible evidence that Google's generative AI prompts, or a large class of them (for example paid API or Workspace prompts), earned more than they cost to serve in the period. Part 2: evidence that Gemini uptake was large relative to Google's reach and to rivals.

evidence.excerpt: in October 2024, Gemini’s user numbers were 9 million daily and 90 million monthly.
evidence.explanation: About 90 million monthly users in October 2024 is a sizeable absolute audience. That cuts against a literal 'nobody cares', though not against the relative reading. Reported from a court exhibit.

evidence.excerpt: Meta AI was nearing 500 million monthly users as of September 2024, while OpenAI recently said that its weekly active users top 400 million.
evidence.explanation: Rivals had several times Gemini's audience around the target period. That supports the relative reading that Gemini uptake was weak given Google's reach.

evidence.excerpt: “We’ve seen for a given query the cost has fallen dramatically in the [past] 18-month time frame.”
evidence.explanation: Pichai says per-query cost fell sharply but gives no cost or revenue figures. It neither confirms nor refutes per-prompt losses.

evidence.excerpt: The most commonly used product was ChatGPT (28 percent) followed by Google Gemini (16 percent).
evidence.explanation: In a US survey from August 2024, just before the target period, Gemini was the second most used generative AI product. That suggests real if secondary interest.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Disclosure or credible reporting of Google's per-prompt (or per-token) serving cost against revenue for Gemini and its other generative AI products in late 2024 or early 2025.
